alternative_architecture.description: The core loop shape (persistent graph → bounded worker → GER with runtime evidence → human merge → evidence-derived completion) does not need to be replaced. The correction needed is sequencing, not architecture: the team should have proven one provider's write-and-merge loop on one real ticket before generalizing to a second provider and before building the full evidence/conformance ceremony around zero exercised dispatches.
alternative_architecture.why_better: n/a — a different architecture is not indicated by the evidence; a different build order is.

structured_output.architecture_summary: The target design is a deterministic-supervisor / bounded-LLM-worker loop: immutable GDD canon → persistent Tasks/*.yaml work graph with deterministic readiness → (planned) targeted RAG context + Progressive Decomposer + Artifact Authority Gate → (planned) supervisor with branch/worktree/Draft-PR claiming → bounded ExecutionCrew (Implementer/Validator) → GER repair loop with Unity runtime evidence as first-class validation → fresh diff review → human merge → dependency recompute. Completion is explicitly separated from mutable task status: Tasks/*.yaml define approved work; immutable delivery/revalidation evidence records plus a deterministic conformance evaluator derive current state (conformant/needs_revalidation/needs_replan/etc.) from committed Git+GDD hashes; a separate, currently hardcoded-denied execution_authority gate is meant to eventually decide dispatch. Only Milestone 1 (persistent graph/taskcontrol) and the Phase 1-3 evidence/conformance correction are implemented; Milestone 2 (RAG/scanner/decomposer/artifact authority), the supervisor, ExecutionCrew, and any repository-write capability for an agent do not exist. The most recent implementation effort (Stage 4A-4D) built a provider-neutral AgentRuntime and migrated the ArchitectureReview meta-tool (not gameplay execution) through both Claude and Codex adapters, with repository read/search only — no write, no command execution, no task-bound execution.
structured_output.biggest_uncertainty: Whether, once write capability and real execution exist, the team will actually pause and validate the loop on one small ticket before adding the next abstraction layer — or whether the demonstrated pattern (choosing meta-work like a second-provider ArchitectureReview migration over the real next execution slice, twice) will continue and keep the pipeline permanently one layer away from shipping gameplay.
do_not_build_yet: Write or command-execution capability for the second provider (Codex) — prove one provider first.
The full 3-role ExecutionCrew (Implementer + Unity Test Author + Validator) — start with a single write-capable role.
Milestone 2's RAG/context-builder/Progressive Decomposer/Artifact Authority Gate platform.
Continuous autonomy loop, task claiming, or any parallel workers.
Any further task-contract schema version or evidence-record type beyond what's already implemented.
Any further ArchitectureReview provider migration, comparison pipeline, or dual-provider launcher.

evidence.observation: Explicitly states repository writing, approved_command_execution, and production ExecutionCrew orchestration remain unsupported; readiness is UNAVAILABLE and authorize is DENIED for all tasks; the 'Immediate Next Goal' completed in this window was migrating the ArchitectureReview meta-tool through AgentRuntime, not any gameplay task.
assess_execution_authorization unconditionally returns authorized=False for any task; there is no real dispatch policy yet, only a fixed denial.

The only historically 'complete' task at bootstrap was NSC-023, and CURRENT_STATE.md separately confirms that completion was pre-pipeline manual work later retrofitted with Phase 3A evidence records, not produced by autonomous execution.

A concrete, well-grounded, GDD-cited task contract with real repository evidence at bootstrap — but CURRENT_STATE.md documents unresolved design questions blocking its assignment, showing 'concrete/single_agent' in the graph does not guarantee the underlying design is actually settled.

States the project's own working rule: 'infrastructure should increasingly be proven by advancing actual No Safe Circle gameplay rather than becoming a separate project that indefinitely delays the game' — a rule the most recent Stage 4 work (dual-provider ArchitectureReview migration) did not follow.

Confirms AgentRuntime's only production consumer so far is the ArchitectureReview meta-review tool itself, run through Docker with a read-only repository mount and no write/command-execution authority for either provider.
ExecutionCrew, ADR-034 production roles, and the actual write-capable Implementer are still described as a target layout/plan, not implemented files.

gdd_iteration_concerns: No cheap, scoped mechanism exists to detect that an already-written but not-yet-implemented task contract (e.g., NSC-003) has drifted from a newer GDD edit; only a full immutable-snapshot reconciliation (multi-model verification crew) is defined, which is too heavyweight to run after every design tweak, contradicting the goal of letting the GDD iterate freely during development.

For already-implemented tasks, the conformance evaluator's needs_revalidation/needs_replan states are a good reactive answer once evidence exists (hash mismatch against current GDD/contract triggers replan), but there is no equivalent proactive signal for open/undelivered work, so stale task contracts can silently persist until a human notices or a full reconciliation is run.

NSC-003 itself is a live example: its task contract is already written and marked single_agent/concrete, yet CURRENT_STATE.md documents open, unresolved design questions (input-action ownership, spell/UI arbitration, movement pathing) that the GDD apparently doesn't yet resolve — meaning the graph can mark work 'ready' before the design underneath it is actually settled.
human_intervention_points: Play Mode / runtime evidence approval before a delivery record counts as conformant (already exercised for NSC-023).
Resolving NSC-003's open design questions (input-action ownership, spell/UI/interaction arbitration, movement pathing) before it can safely be handed to any worker.
Artifact Authority Gate NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW outcomes (mechanism exists conceptually, not yet exercised).
Reviewing and applying any reconciliation-proposed graph delta.
Designing and approving the dispatch-authorization policy itself before execution_authority can ever return true.
PR/diff review and merge for every ticket (by design, no automatic merge).
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Task-contract schema 2.0 migration removing mutable status fields, plus the full evidence-record/conformance-evaluator apparatus (delivery/baseline/revalidation records, ancestry checks, ambiguous-evidence detection) — responds to a failure mode a prior architecture review predicted (mutable metadata mistaken for completion truth), not one this project has actually hit, since no autonomous dispatch has ever occurred.

Provider-neutral dual-adapter AgentRuntime with strict capability-mapping enforcement (approved_command_execution, non-null token_limit fail-closed, etc.) for capabilities that are not yet used by any production consumer.
Fail-closed execution_authority stub as a standing 'zero tasks may be dispatched' gate, guarding against dispatch that cannot currently occur under any code path anyway.

Migrating the ArchitectureReview review tool itself through the new generic runtime for two providers before any gameplay consumer exists, primarily to preserve future Claude-vs-Codex comparison capability that is explicitly not yet implemented or needed.
missing_components: Any agent repository-write or approved-command-execution capability — the actual bottleneck for leverage.
ExecutionCrew role implementations (Implementer/Validator/Unity Test Author) — currently only planned in a document.
The supervisor loop — currently pseudocode only, not implemented.

Milestone 2: RAG/context builder wiring into task execution, project scanner, Progressive Decomposer, Artifact Authority Gate — none implemented; NSC-003 and similar tasks cannot yet receive a compact context pack.
A scoped/local GDD-change-impact-analysis mechanism cheap enough to run after routine GDD edits (only full multi-model reconciliation exists today, which is heavyweight).

deliverables: Add a minimal write capability to the existing Claude AgentRuntime provider, scoped to an explicit path allowlist (reuse the task's exclusive_resources list as the allowlist) using the same fail-closed capability-mapping pattern already built for read/search.

A minimal single-ticket runner: create a branch, invoke one Implementer-role AgentRuntime call with write capability restricted to the allowlist, run the existing Pipeline/Testing/run_unity_tests_clean.ps1, stop. Do not build the full 3-role ExecutionCrew, worktree automation, or Draft-PR automation yet.

Select the smallest, least design-ambiguous ready task from the existing frontier (e.g. NSC-037 Windows Build Scene Registration or NSC-024 Tilemap/AI Navigation Package Configuration) rather than NSC-003, which still has open human design questions.
A human-reviewed merge, and — only if it passes — a genuine Phase 3 delivery evidence record generated by the pipeline itself rather than added after manual work.
next_slice.proof_of_value: The first real repository change produced end-to-end by an autonomous agent invocation, validated by existing deterministic Unity tooling, and merged — actual evidence the pipeline saves developer time, as opposed to only auditing and reviewing itself.
next_slice.title: Prove one real write-capable ticket end-to-end before adding any further abstraction
next_slice.why: Two days of intensive engineering have produced extensive governance/evidence/multi-provider machinery but zero autonomously-written, merged gameplay code. The single highest-leverage next step is not more schema, evidence, or provider generalization — it is making one provider able to write a small, tightly-scoped change and proving the full loop (invoke → write → deterministic Unity validation → human review → merge → evidence record produced by the pipeline itself, not retrofitted) actually works on real work.

observed_failure_solutions: GER + mandatory runtime evidence for interactive/visual/timing-sensitive Unity behavior, because Assignment 6's camera passed static evaluation while being unusable at runtime (ADR-015).
No-op refinement counts as a failed repair attempt against budget, because Assignment 6 observed a Refiner claiming 'implemented' with zero changes under Assets/ (ADR-016).
Validation evidence bundles rather than a single PASS/FAIL source, because the camera loop only succeeded once Unity observations re-entered the same repair loop (ADR-017).
overengineering: Dual-provider (Claude + Codex) AgentRuntime and dual ArchitectureReview migrations before a single provider has any write or execution capability.
Task-contract schema 2.0 + migration tooling + quality audit + a 12-scenario conformance-evidence regression suite for a system that has completed zero autonomously-executed tasks.
Capability/enforcement hardening for provider features (command execution, token limits) that no current consumer requests.
Spending a governance/meta-tool (ArchitectureReview) build-out cycle on itself (this review) rather than on the production execution path it exists to gate.
state_and_authority_concerns: The four-layer authority stack (task definition → evidence records → derived conformance → execution-authority gate) is conceptually sound but entirely unvalidated by any real dispatch; it risks becoming ceremony that consumes engineering time without yet protecting anything, since nothing can currently be dispatched.

execution_authority.py is a static denial function, not a policy; designing the real readiness∧conformant∧approved→authorize policy remains fully未done and is nontrivial future work, distinct from the scaffolding already built around it.

The reconciliation diff/review/apply boundary (ADR-026) is documented and produces PROPOSED_GRAPH_DELTA artifacts, but I did not verify a deterministic apply-enforcement code path in this pass; that boundary's enforcement is asserted more than directly confirmed in code I inspected.
strong_decisions: Deterministic supervisor owns the loop; the LLM is a bounded, replaceable worker per ticket (ADR-002) — correct allocation of judgment vs. computation.

Persistent Tasks/*.yaml graph with deterministic readiness calculation (Milestone 1) is actually implemented, validated against the real 37-record graph, and produces a truthful ready frontier without an LLM.

Bootstrap used immutable point-in-time reconciliation plus independent multi-model verification with unioned (not majority-voted) findings before human approval — a genuinely rigorous provenance chain for seed data.

GER treated as a general bounded-repair pattern, not just a content-generation gate, directly following from an observed failure (Assignment 6 camera passing static checks while failing at runtime) — ADR-010/015/016/017 are evidence-grounded, not speculative.
Explicit separation of artifact authority (may this be invented at all) from artifact quality (is it good) prevents an implementer from silently becoming a game designer.
Reconciliation is treated as an immutable snapshot rather than a mutable truth source, with graph changes crossing an explicit diff/review/apply boundary rather than direct LLM rewrites.

Evidence-derived conformance reads only committed Git/GDD state and explicitly ignores uncommitted working-tree content, which was directly demonstrated (NSC-023 flipped from not_delivered to conformant only after committing evidence).
structural_flaws: No repository-write or command-execution capability exists anywhere in AgentRuntime; the entire elaborate evidence/conformance/authority stack sits on top of a system that cannot yet cause any code to be written by an agent, so none of it has been exercised under real autonomous execution.

Sequencing inversion: the team generalized to two providers (Claude+Codex) and migrated a meta-governance tool (ArchitectureReview) through that generic runtime before proving a single-provider, single-ticket write-and-merge loop, contradicting the project's own stated 'do not build later layers before the single-task path is trustworthy' rule.

The execution_authority gate is currently a hardcoded blanket denial (assess_execution_authorization always returns authorized=False) rather than a real policy; the actual dispatch-authorization design (the thing that matters once write capability exists) has not been designed at all, only deferred.
structured_output.throughput_assessment: Not yet demonstrated. Since the pipeline's task graph was bootstrapped (2026-08-21) through the most recent work (2026-08-23), zero gameplay features have been produced by the pipeline; the only 'production proof' (NSC-023) evidences pre-existing manually-built work retrofitted with evidence records after the fact. All measured engineering throughput in this window went into meta-infrastructure (schema migration, evidence model, dual-provider AgentRuntime, ArchitectureReview migration) rather than shipped gameplay. Any claim that this architecture will make development 'days instead of weeks' is currently speculative; the system has not yet been used to write a single line of production code autonomously.
structured_output.verdict_reason: The core control-loop shape (persistent graph → bounded worker → GER with runtime evidence → human merge → evidence-derived, not self-declared, completion) is coherent and not architecturally wrong; nothing I found is a structural dead end. But the project has spent roughly two days of intensive engineering (task-contract schema 2.0 + migration + quality audit, a full evidence/conformance record model with 12 regression scenarios, a fail-closed execution-authority stub, and a dual-provider AgentRuntime) without ever exercising the one capability that actually matters for "days instead of weeks": an agent writing code against a task and getting it merged. The only completed "gameplay" evidence (NSC-023) was implemented outside the pipeline and retrofitted with evidence records; the only production use of the brand-new AgentRuntime so far is running the ArchitectureReview meta-tool on itself, twice, across two providers. The team's own documented principle ("infrastructure must quickly feed real game implementation," "avoid building later autonomous layers speculatively before the preceding single-task path has proven reliable") has been violated by its own most recent choices. This is a sequencing/overbuilding problem, not a soundness problem.
